notes.title: ArmaCulture Release Patch 2
notes.content:
Hello again! 

Originally I wasn't sure I was going to do this, but after a lot of thought I think its a necessary feature. 

This patch introduces an assist mode to the game, accessible after going Bankrupt from the Game Over screen. This mode allows players to retry the day they lost on but with 1000 in extra money on top of what they had. However, if the players does so, the rest of their run will be stuck in assist mode- meaning you will be immediately locked out of any ending besides the neutral one. (Assist is only accessible on normal mode, however.) 

I decided to do this mostly to address the players that were interested in the story but found the game play to be too challenging. I think that through this option players will be able to practice for their future runs as well. 

As always, please let me know if you have any questions or concerns. That's all for now.

RageForDragons

notes.title: ArmaCulture Release Patch 1
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

I'm glad to see that people are enjoying the full game. I've identified a number of things over the past few weeks that I decided should get a change (some of them I've already introduced, sorry for the confusion). 

In no particular order, here is what this patch has changed:

[list]
[*] Numerous grammatical errors
[*] Fixed the trade offer in the tutorial so its addressed to the correct person (haha) 
[*] Added in a number of hints on day 1 to help ease in new players, including a checklist of things to work on and indicators as to how the farm should be built 
[*] Fixed a large issue with the endings/routes system, which now prevents players from seeing cut scenes intended to be viewed only after having seen all the previous ones 
[*] Updated several character sprites to reflect the newer art style better
[*] Other minor interaction/animation changes 
[/list]

As always, please let me know if you come across bugs or other things that don't seem right. Thanks for playing!

notes.title: ArmaCulture Chapter III | OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

I know it's been a [i]very long wait[/i] (a lot longer than I had hoped, any way) but its finally here nonetheless. ArmaCulture is finally finished, and its finally time for me to share it with everyone. 

Thank you so much for your patience, I really hope that it was worth the wait. Here is what to expect with the new version of the game:

- 15 in game weeks with many new interactions, machines, and events.
- The full story line with over 35 fully illustrated cut scenes with new music. 
- Major quality of life changes to nearly everything
- A functioning tutorial (lol) 
- 3 Distinct 'routes' based on your reputation that significantly alter the course of events and endings. 
- A full 25 track OST 
- Steam Achievements

In addition to the game and new trailer, I have also just released the update to the OST, expanding it to the new 25 track length. If you owned the OST before, it will automatically update for free! 

Its a very exciting day for me getting to finally see this project through after nearly two years. I really hope you enjoy what I've made.

As always, thanks for playing.

- ragefordragons

notes.title: ArmaCulture Chapter III - Update Progress Report
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I've been working hard on ArmaCulture over the past weeks, and I'd like to share what is complete as of now, and what still needs to be done. Hopefully, I will also be able to provide a clearer timeline for the release date. The thumbnail is a small preview of some of the new war story art. 

[b]As of August 15th, 2021 I have completed the following for ArmaCulture Chapter III (That's what I'm calling this update):
[/b]
[list]
[*] All of the normal interactions for the last five days, including three distinct final interactions depending on the reputation route the player has chosen. 
[*] Major changes to the factory system, including electricity and the shipping limit. 
[*] Third shopkeeper, from which you can increase your shipping limit.
[*] Steam achievements implemented. (You might be able to see them in your library, but you won't be able to unlock them until the update is released.) 
[*] Major menu and UI overhaul throughout the game.
[*] Added postprocessing. 
[*] New cutscenes during the course of the game.
[*] Updates to all the war stories, adding new art and majorly improving old art. 
[*] New extra's menu with access to game stats, war stories, and challenge modes.
[*] Several new songs to accompany the new interactions and eventually new war stories. 
[*] Script for one (very long) new war story is written, and I have planned out the other. 
[*] Difficulty system added.
[/list]

[b]And here is what I still need to do:
[/b]
[list]
[*] Ending cutscenes (three for three routes.) 
[*] Character art for new interactions and shopkeeper.
[*] Program challenge modes.
[*] Better tutorial. 
[*] Art for new war stories. 
[*] Add a way for the player to earn medals in the course of playing (they will be used to unlock not just new war stories but also challenge modes and other rewards.)
[*] Add additional hard mode challenges.
[/list]

I'm sure I forgot a few, but that's the idea. I'm making good progress, and I'm predicting that the update will be finished in just under 1.5 to 2 months- as long as I don't get too busy with life in the meantime. Thanks for your patience- I am very excited to show everyone the new version of the game and I can safely say it is a large improvement over the last. 

Any questions? Feel free to leave them in the comments section.
Thanks for playing ArmaCulture!

notes.title: The Future Of ArmaCulture
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

I'd like to say that first I am very humbled by the positive reception ArmaCulture has received so far. Not to mention the constructive feedback that everyone has left me- it is always helpful in order to grow as a developer. 

I figured now was a good time to let everyone know what my plans are for the future of this project. 

As is, ArmaCulture is obviously incomplete. Ideally I would like there to be one more major update, that being the update that finishes the game campaign-wise, irons out the previous material, and overall refines the experience to make it feel more 'finished.' I can't think of a good way to format this, so Instead I'm going to create a laundry list of things I'd like for there to be in that final product. 

Here it is:
[list]
[*] Five more days/nights to have the game end on the 30th of October.
[*] (At least) Five more interactions, preferably 8-9 more to make each new game feel more fresh.
[*] Three different endings, given based on your overall reputation at the end. 
[*] Higher teirs of research, including an overall re-balance of unlocks. 
[*] Re-done art for a few of the not-so-good looking older sprites. (Character portraits as well.)
[*] More War Stories, as well as an extra challenge mode** for progress in the campaign.
[*] Steam Achievements.
[*] Overhauled UI for the title screen, menus.
[*] Difficulty tiers (Including a harder mode for veteran players and a mode that allows you to slow down time.)
[*] A more robust, integrated tutorial. 
[*] Re-balance of the town, as well as adding a third shop keeper.
[*] Adding a use for that currently unused third reputation meter (lol)
[*] More music, perhaps some touch ups on old songs. 
[*] Overall balances, bug fixes.
[*] Finally finish drones. 
[/list]

** The challenge mode is something I already have nearly finished, and I was considering releasing it soon, although it would take some more work. Think of it as a side arcade mode that allows you to test your speed at factory building. If this is something anyone is very interesting in having sooner, let me know. 

[b]TIMELINE[/b]

So what is the timeline for this? I'll be upfront and say I don't have a solid idea at the moment. From the first demo on Gamejolt to the version you all have now on Steam, it took about 2 months of work, but that was because the previous 6-8 months had been spent getting the basic systems and core game play set up. To finish this game as ambitiously as I intend to above, I am expecting at least 4 or 5 months of work. However, my personal life is becoming increasingly busy and I can't promise I will be able to work on the game as quickly as I was in the past. Not to mention the fact that I've been taking a break from development on the game, and I still need more time to recoup. All in all, its going to be a bit of a wait, that much is certain. 

So that's all for now. 

Please, let me know in the comments what you would like to see in the final version of this game. If there is anything here you'd like to know more about, feel free to ask. I want to make sure not to disappoint. 

Thank you for playing!
